course: Cosmetics: Lip Balms, Body Butters & Hair Oils

lessons.title: Using WhatsApp and Facebook to Sell
lessons.body:
WhatsApp and Facebook are the most powerful free tools for selling your cosmetics in Africa. Start by creating a WhatsApp Business account (download the app, select 'Business' when setting up). Set your profile photo to your best product image, write a clear description like 'Handmade lip balms, body butters & hair oils â Nairobi delivery', and add your business hours. Use the catalog feature to list each product with a photo, price, and short description. For example, 'Shea Body Butter 250ml â KES 800'.

On Facebook, create a Business Page (not a personal profile). Post 3â4 times a week. Use a mix of product photos, customer testimonials, and behind-the-scenes videos of you making the products. Join local buy/sell groups (e.g., 'Nairobi Buy and Sell', 'Accra Market'). Post your products there with a clear price and a call to action like 'DM to order'. Always respond to comments and messages within 1 hour â speed builds trust.

Use WhatsApp Status to show daily specials, new stock, or happy customers. Post a photo of a customer using your product with their permission. Offer a 'WhatsApp-only' discount: 'Order via WhatsApp today and get 10% off'. For payments, use mobile money like M-Pesa, MTN MoMo, or Airtel Money. Send a payment confirmation screenshot to the customer. For delivery, use local courier services like Bolt Send, Uber Connect, or boda boda riders. Charge a flat delivery fee (e.g., KES 200 within the city).

Keep a simple customer list in your phone contacts â add a tag like 'Cosmetics Customer'. Every Friday, send a broadcast message to your list with a weekend special. But don't spam; once a week is enough. Ask satisfied customers to send a voice note or text testimonial you can share. A simple 'I love your body butter!' screenshot on your status can bring 5 new orders. Remember: consistency beats perfection. Post every day, even if it's just a short video of you mixing shea butter.

lessons.title: Taking Product Photos with a Smartphone
lessons.body:
You don't need an expensive camera. A smartphone with a good camera (even a 12MP one) is enough. The key is lighting and background. Natural daylight is best â take photos near a window between 10am and 2pm, but avoid direct sunlight which creates harsh shadows. If you're outside, find a shaded area with bright indirect light. Never use flash â it makes products look greasy and washed out.

Create a simple backdrop. Use a plain white or light grey cloth, a wooden board, or a clean wall. For lip balms, place them on a small white plate or a piece of slate. For body butter jars, use a wooden spoon or fresh leaves (like mint or aloe) as props. For hair oils, use a dropper and a small towel. Keep it clean â no clutter. Wipe the jar edges with a tissue before shooting.

Shooting angles: take at least 5 photos per product â one straight-on, one from 45 degrees, one top-down (flat lay), one close-up of the texture (open the jar), and one in your hand to show size. Use the grid feature on your phone camera to keep lines straight. Tap on the product to focus, then slide the exposure bar down slightly to avoid overexposure. For a professional look, use a free app like Snapseed or Lightroom Mobile to adjust brightness, contrast, and warmth. Don't over-edit â keep colors true to life.

For video, record a 15-second clip: open the jar, scoop a little product, rub it on your skin. Show the texture. Use natural sound â no music needed. If you want music, use royalty-free tracks from the app. Save photos in a folder named 'Product Photos'. Use the same style for all products so your brand looks consistent. A good photo can increase sales by 30% because customers buy with their eyes first. Practice once a week â take 10 photos, pick the best 3, and delete the rest.

lessons.title: Writing Compelling Product Descriptions
lessons.body:
A good product description answers three questions: What is it? What does it do? Why should I buy from you? Write in simple English or a mix of English and local language (like Swahili, Pidgin, or Zulu) to connect with your audience. Start with a strong headline: 'Raw Shea Body Butter â Deep Moisture for Dry Skin' instead of just 'Body Butter'.

Use the AIDA formula: Attention, Interest, Desire, Action. For example: 'Attention: Tired of ashy skin? Interest: Our whipped shea butter is made with 100% raw shea from Northern Ghana. Desire: It melts into your skin, leaving it soft for 24 hours â no greasy feel. Action: Order today on WhatsApp and get free delivery in Accra.' Keep it short â 50 to 100 words per product. Use bullet points for ingredients and benefits: 'Ingredients: Raw shea butter, coconut oil, vitamin E. Benefits: Heals dry elbows, stretch marks, and cracked heels.'

Add social proof: 'Over 200 satisfied customers' or 'As seen on NTV's Morning Show'. Include size and price clearly: '250ml jar â KES 800'. Mention delivery options: 'Same-day delivery in Nairobi, next-day upcountry.' Use urgency: 'Only 10 jars left this week' or 'Order before Friday for free sample'.

Avoid vague words like 'best' or 'amazing' without proof. Instead, say 'clinically proven to reduce dryness in 7 days' â but only if true. Write like you talk. Read it aloud â if it sounds like a robot, rewrite it. Test different descriptions: post two versions on Facebook and see which gets more orders. Keep a notebook of phrases customers use, like 'my skin feels like silk' â use those in your descriptions. Finally, always include a clear call to action: 'DM 'BUTTER' to order' or 'Click the link in bio'. A strong description can double your conversion rate.

lessons.title: Attending Local Markets and Trade Fairs
lessons.body:
Local markets and trade fairs are the fastest way to get face-to-face sales and feedback. In Nigeria, look for markets like Balogun or Onitsha Main Market; in Kenya, try Maasai Market or Gikomba; in South Africa, Rosebank Sunday Market. Trade fairs like the Lagos International Trade Fair or Nairobi's Kenya Trade Expo attract thousands of buyers. Book a stall early â costs range from KES 1,000 to KES 5,000 per day. For a small table at a community market, you might pay only KES 500.

Prepare your stall: use a bright tablecloth (yellow or orange stands out), arrange products by category (lip balms in front, body butters behind, hair oils on the side). Put up a banner with your business name and WhatsApp number. Have testers â small jars of body butter and lip balm for people to try. Bring a mirror, hand sanitizer, and tissue. Price clearly with stickers: 'Lip Balm â KES 200', 'Body Butter â KES 800'. Offer a market special: 'Buy 2, get 1 free' or 'Free sample with every purchase'.

Engage customers: stand up, smile, and greet everyone. Ask 'Have you tried raw shea butter before?' instead of 'Can I help you?' Give a small sample of hair oil on their hand. Tell your story: 'I make these in my kitchen using ingredients from local farmers.' Collect phone numbers: 'Would you like a free sample next time? Just give me your WhatsApp number.' Use a notebook or a Google Form on your phone.

After the market, send a thank-you message to everyone who bought or gave their number. Offer a 10% discount for their next order if they order within a week. Track what sells best â if lip balms run out first, make more next time. Markets also help you test prices: if many people say 'too expensive', adjust. If no one buys, your display or pitch needs work. Aim to cover your stall fee and make at least 3x profit. Even if you break even, the customer list and feedback are worth it.

lessons.title: Collaborating with Local Influencers
lessons.body:
Local influencers â even those with 1,000 to 10,000 followers â can boost your sales quickly. In Africa, nano-influencers (1kâ10k followers) often charge less (or accept free products) and have high engagement. Look for influencers in your city who post about beauty, natural hair, or skincare. Search Instagram and TikTok with hashtags like #NairobiBeauty, #AccraSkincare, #NaturalHairNigeria. Check their comments â if they reply to followers, they're good to work with.

Start with a direct message: 'Hi [Name], I love your posts on natural hair. I make raw shea hair oils and would love to send you a free sample. If you like it, would you be open to a paid post?' Offer a simple deal: free product + KES 2,000â5,000 for one Instagram post and 3 stories. For TikTok, offer KES 3,000â7,000 for a 15-second video. If budget is tight, offer affiliate commission: 'Use my code [NAME] and get 10% off. You earn 20% of each sale.' Give them a unique code so you can track sales.

Before sending product, agree on deliverables: one post, three stories, one reel, and a swipe-up link to your WhatsApp. Ask them to show the product in use â not just hold it. For example, a hair oil influencer should apply it to their scalp and show the shine. Provide a script if needed: 'I've been using this raw shea hair oil for two weeks and my edges are growing back.' But let them use their own words â authenticity sells.

After the post, monitor sales using the code. Send a thank-you message and a small bonus if sales exceed 10 orders. Build a long-term relationship: send free products monthly in exchange for one post. This is cheaper than ads. Also, collaborate with micro-influencers who are not yet famous â they are hungry and affordable. Always ask for a screenshot of insights (reach, likes, comments) to measure success. A good influencer can bring 20â50 orders in a week.

lessons.title: Building Customer Loyalty with Free Samples
lessons.body:
Free samples are not a cost â they are an investment. A small 5ml lip balm or 10ml hair oil sample costs you less than KES 50 to make, but it can turn a first-time buyer into a repeat customer. Include a free sample with every order. For example, if someone buys a 250ml body butter, add a tiny lip balm with a handwritten note: 'Enjoy this free gift! Love, [Your Name]'. This personal touch makes customers feel special and more likely to order again.

Use samples strategically at markets and pop-ups. Give a sample only after they show interest â not to everyone passing by. Ask: 'Would you like to try our new mango lip balm?' Then hand it over with a smile. Collect their WhatsApp number: 'I'll send you a special discount for your first full-size order.' Follow up within 48 hours: 'Hi [Name], did you enjoy the sample? Here's 15% off your first jar â valid for 3 days.' This converts 30â40% of sample recipients into buyers.

Create a loyalty program: after 5 purchases, give a free full-size product. Track purchases in a notebook or a simple Google Sheet. Send a WhatsApp message: 'Congratulations! You've earned a free hair oil. Claim it with your next order.' Also, ask for referrals: 'Give a sample to a friend. When they order, you both get 10% off.' This turns customers into salespeople.

For online orders, include a sample of a different product to encourage cross-selling. If they bought body butter, send a hair oil sample. Many will come back to buy the full size. Keep samples fresh â make small batches weekly. Use small jars or sachets (you can buy 100 sachets for KES 300). Label each sample with your WhatsApp number and a short message: 'Love this? Order full size at [number]'. Finally, follow up after 7 days: 'How was your sample? Any feedback?' Feedback helps you improve and shows you care. Loyal customers spend 5x more over their lifetime, so samples pay off.

quiz.q: What is the first step to using WhatsApp for business?
options: A) Create a WhatsApp Business account
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp Business offers catalog, auto-replies, and business profile features needed for selling.

quiz.q: How often should you post on your Facebook Business Page?
options: D) Only when you have new stock
quiz.explanation: Consistent posting 3â4 times a week keeps your audience engaged without spamming.

quiz.q: Which mobile money service is commonly used in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: M-Pesa is Kenya's leading mobile money platform for payments.

quiz.q: What is a good time to take product photos using natural light?
options: D) Any time with direct sunlight
quiz.explanation: Indirect daylight between 10am and 2pm gives bright, even lighting without harsh shadows.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid using flash when photographing cosmetics?
options: B) It makes products look greasy and washed out
D) It is not allowed on phones
quiz.explanation: Flash creates harsh reflections that make oils and butters look unappealing.

quiz.q: How many photos per product should you aim to take?
quiz.explanation: Five angles (straight, 45Â°, top-down, close-up, in-hand) give a complete view.

quiz.q: What is the AIDA formula used for?
quiz.explanation: AIDA (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) structures persuasive product descriptions.

quiz.q: What should a strong product headline include?
options: B) A benefit and key ingredient
quiz.explanation: Headlines like 'Raw Shea Body Butter â Deep Moisture for Dry Skin' combine ingredient and benefit.

quiz.q: Why is social proof important in descriptions?
options: A) It makes the description longer
B) It builds trust with potential buyers
C) It is required by law
D) It helps with SEO only
quiz.explanation: Testimonials and customer counts reassure buyers that others have had good experiences.

quiz.q: What is a good call to action for a WhatsApp order?
quiz.explanation: A specific keyword like 'BUTTER' makes it easy for customers to start an order.

quiz.q: Where can you find local markets to sell cosmetics in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Maasai Market is a well-known craft and goods market in Kenya.

quiz.q: What should you bring to a market stall for customers to try?
quiz.explanation: Testers allow customers to experience the product, increasing purchase likelihood.

quiz.q: How can you collect customer contacts at a market?
options: A) Ask for their WhatsApp number
B) Take a photo of their ID
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp numbers let you follow up with offers and build a customer list.

quiz.q: What is a good market special to boost sales?
quiz.explanation: Bundled offers encourage larger purchases and move stock faster.

quiz.q: What should you do after a market day?
options: B) Send thank-you messages to buyers
D) Wait for customers to call
quiz.explanation: Follow-up builds relationships and encourages repeat business.

quiz.q: What is a nano-influencer?
quiz.explanation: Nano-influencers have smaller but highly engaged audiences and are affordable.

quiz.q: What is a common payment for a nano-influencer post?
quiz.explanation: Nano-influencers often accept a combination of free product and a small fee.

quiz.q: What should you agree on before sending product to an influencer?
quiz.explanation: Clear deliverables (posts, stories, reels) ensure you get value for your product.

quiz.q: How can you track sales from an influencer?
options: A) Give them a unique discount code
quiz.explanation: A unique code lets you see exactly how many orders came from that influencer.

quiz.q: What is a good way to build long-term influencer relationships?
quiz.explanation: Regular free products keep influencers motivated to post about your brand.

quiz.q: Why are free samples a good investment?
options: B) They turn first-time buyers into repeat customers
D) They are required by law
quiz.explanation: Samples let customers experience the product, increasing loyalty and repeat purchases.

quiz.q: What size sample is suggested for a lip balm?
quiz.explanation: A 5ml sample is enough for a few uses and costs very little to produce.

quiz.q: How soon should you follow up after giving a sample?
quiz.explanation: A quick follow-up with a discount converts interest into a sale.

quiz.q: What is a loyalty program reward?
options: B) A discount on first purchase
quiz.explanation: Rewarding repeat purchases with a free full-size product encourages loyalty.

quiz.q: How can you encourage referrals?
options: A) Give a sample to a friend and both get 10% off
quiz.explanation: Referral incentives turn happy customers into active promoters.

quiz.q: What should you include on a sample label?
quiz.explanation: A WhatsApp number makes it easy for sample recipients to order full sizes.

quiz.q: Why is it important to ask for feedback after a sample?
options: A) It shows you care and helps improve
B) It is required by law
quiz.explanation: Feedback builds relationship and gives you insights to refine your products.

quiz.q: What is a good way to use WhatsApp Status for sales?
options: A) Post daily specials and customer photos
B) Post only once a month
quiz.explanation: Regular status updates keep your products visible and top-of-mind.

quiz.q: What is a flat delivery fee example within a city?
quiz.explanation: A flat fee like KES 200 is simple and covers typical local courier costs.

quiz.q: What should you do if many customers say your product is 'too expensive' at a market?
options: A) Adjust your price or offer smaller sizes
quiz.explanation: Market feedback helps you find the right price point or packaging.
